title: Good for small steaming jobs but not the quality I would expect had I purchased this at the list price
text:
Good for small steaming jobs but not the quality I would expect had I purchased this at the list price. I'm a steamer fanatic and selected this because I'm crazy about steamers. In fact, I've owned 10 steamers in total. Since 2 broke, I now own 8 steamers with the receipt of this one.

This is a tiny steamer that works well for small steaming jobs. The broccoli I steamed came out beautiful. I filled the pot to the halfway point with boiling water, set the steamer basket on top with the broccoli, and covered the steamer basket. Once the water came to a boil (about 9 minutes in), I steamed the broccoli for 8 minutes until it was softened but still firm and a rich green color. However, despite my successful results, to me this steamer is just okay for the below reasons.

PROS

- It's great for steaming a small quantity of vegetables.

- It has a small footprint of 6-1/2 inches at the widest point on the bottom. However, if you include the handles, it's 11 inches wide by 11 inches tall.

- The red gradient color is attractive.

- The stainless steel basket feels sturdy (see comment in CON section).

- The steamer basket is 3-3/4 inches deep.

- The handles are comfortable and stay cool.

- The pot and lid can be used without the steamer basket and the lid fit securely on top.

CONS

- The steamer basket is really too small for family-sized steaming jobs where large quantities of items need to be steamed. The basket is not wide enough to steam a whole unbroken ear of corn. Corn would have to be broken in half and steamed vertically to get the most out of the space.

- The pot feels cheap. Although, the pot can be used as a regular cooking pot with lid without the steamer insert, I do not feel it will wear well.

- After steaming my broccoli, the steamer basket became convex. I had to push the bottom of the steamer basket back in place so that it would sit flat on my counter. However, to me this particular behavior of the basket is unimportant as most of the time the steamer basket sits on top of the pot, so I don't care if it's a bit wobbly.

- I put 3 quarts of water in the pot and the water was even with the top, so figure on getting no more than 2 or 2-1/2 quarts of cooking liquid in this pot for cooking purposes.
.
- I think the current price of $50.97 is a bit too expensive for this steamer. The maximum I would pay is half that.

- The pot is not dishwasher safe because it has a porcelain enamel-exterior. I don't care about this but others might be concerned.

- Although the packaging says this unit is safe for ceramic or glass stovetops, the product insert specifically states that they recommend the use of flat-bottomed stainless steel or hard-anodized exterior cookware on ceramic/glass cooktops because overheating porcelain enameled cookware or letting it boil dry can result in the fusing of the cookware to the stove requiring replacement of the stovetop.

Facts about the steamer as stated on the product packaging:
- The handles are oven safe to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
- The 3-quart pot has a non-stick interior and a hard enamel exterior.
- The steamer basket is stainless steel.
- The pan and steamer insert are made in Thailand; the lid is made in China.
- The entire unit has a lifetime limited warranty.
- The entire unit is suitable for glass/ceramic (see comment in CONS section), gas, and electric stoves

In summary, I think this steamer is good for small cooking or steaming jobs. It's a cute little steamer that has a relatively small but tall footprint. However, based on the cons above and the fact that I do not believe the quality of the pot is as good as it could be, I'm rating this as just okay.

For those who are interested, below is a list of MY STEAMERS - PAST and PRESENT

PAST 2 STEAMERS:
--> One small round Black and Decker Steamer (extinct now) which was great but only lasted about two years. This was my first steamer that I got in the mid-90's.
--> One Krups Optisteam Plus (viewable on Amazon at this link - [[ASIN:B00004SPEI Krups 652 70 OptiSteam 2 Tier Steamer]] but for some reason not searchable on Amazon by name). I had this since February 1999 and it was my most used steamer but I thought it was just a tad large for everyday single person use. It just broke.

CURRENT 8 STEAMERS (not counting one steamer insert for small pots):

-->This steamer ([[ASIN:B00E62ERJS Rachael Ray Porcelain Enamel II Nonstick Covered Steamer Set, 3-Quart, Red Gradient]]
--> One [[ASIN:B008FX6KH6 T-fal VC133851 Balanced Living Compact Electric Food Steamer, 4-Quart, Silver]]
--> One [[ASIN:B00073HLMU Oster 5711 Mechanical Food Steamer]] which I used daily for my oatmeal and most dinners.
--> Two [[ASIN:B000JJMER4 Richard Simmons EST7 Steam-Heat Electronic Food Steamer]]s which I absolutely love. But they are very large and good for steaming full meals.
--> One rice steamer, the [[ASIN:B00007J5U7 Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 5-1/2-Cup Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer, Premium White]], which is excellent but that I don't use nearly enough. It's also a little different that these plastic steamers in function.
--> One [[ASIN:B003NTXFVG 14" Hard Anodized Non-Stick Wok with Steamer and Lid]]
--> One Stove-top fish steamer similar to the [[ASIN:B0002IBJG4 Norpro Stainless Steel Fish Poacher]]

product_metadata.title: Rachael Ray Brights Sauce Pot/Saucepot with Steamer Insert, 3 Quart, Orange Gradient
features: CONVENIENT MULTI POT: Make soups and stews with this nonstick saucepot or add the steamer basket for seafood, pasta, or corn on the cob
MADE TO LAST: Durable aluminum saucepot with steam basket heats quickly and evenly for convenient cooking
EASY DOES IT: Long-lasting nonstick easily releases foods for stovetop convenience and fast cleanup
GET A GRIP: Grippy handles are comfortable to grasp and double riveted for extra strength when using the steamer set as a pasta pot or lobster pot
OVEN LOVIN': Oven safe to 350°F, this saucepot and steamer combo is a great addition for versatility in your kitchen
SET INCLUDES: 3-Quart Saucepot, Stainless Steel Steamer Insert and Lid
description: Steam your way to meal time success with this multipurpose steamer set. Vegetables, dumplings and tamales steam to perfection in no time and the steamer insert makes it a cinch to boil and strain pasta for a delicious spaghetti dinner. The saucepot is perfect on its own for making stews, soups, and sauces, too. High-quality nonstick for easy food release and fast cleanup. Oven safe to 350°F.
